meta.name: Acme
meta.title: One ecosystem, two clearly separated platforms
meta.intro: Acme runs a consumer marketplace and a business platform on two independent application stacks, sharing a single operational core.
meta.distributionNote: Every component belongs to exactly one scope of responsibility.
meta.principle: Guiding principle. The consumer and business platforms share neither back-office nor database. They meet only on the shared core.

sections.title: Two platforms, one ecosystem
sections.subtitle: The separation is structural: stacks, databases and deployment cycles are independent.

columns.title: Consumer marketplace
columns.pitch: The real-time journey: order, assign, execute, deliver — within the hour.
bullets: Short cycle: the constraint is assignment latency and ETA accuracy.
Billing and refunds handled directly in the consumer API.

columns.title: Business platform
columns.pitch: The contractual journey: quote, contract, SLA, invoicing — over days.
bullets: Long cycle: the constraint is traceability and milestone reliability.
The CMS is the back-office of the B2B platform, the CRM and the field app.

cards.title: The shared core
cards.subtitle: The only components genuinely common to both platforms.
bullets: Redis — cache, queues and event bus.
Object storage — proofs, media, documents.
CRM / ERP — unified commercial view.
Field app — execution for both platforms.
Infrastructure — containers, proxy, CI/CD, observability.

sections.title: Infrastructure, security & operations
sections.subtitle: A deliberately simple, containerised and observable foundation shared by both platforms.

items.title: Hosting & containers
bullets: Dedicated VMs, DNS per subdomain, delegation per environment.
Docker for every application service.
Persistent volumes for databases and cache.

items.title: Authentication & API
bullets: OAuth2 / JWT, key rotation, short sessions.
Optional MFA on back-offices.
Rate limiting, webhook signatures, strict CORS.

items.title: Data & compliance
bullets: Encryption at rest and in transit.
PII masking in logs, controlled retention.
Secrets via environment variables, audit logs.

items.title: Observability & SRE
bullets: Centralised logs, correlation by traceId.
API latency, error rate, queue depth, delivery rate.
Alerting on SLA thresholds and resource saturation.

sections.title: Next 12 weeks
sections.subtitle: Three phases, plus two structural workstreams.

items.title: Foundations
bullets: Map the top 20 support tickets into guided self-service journeys.
Unify transactional messaging templates across both platforms.

items.title: Event bus & telemetry
bullets: Publish domain events to the internal bus.
Wire every notification trigger to the bus — one source of truth.
Ship a "Service Health" dashboard.

items.title: Self-service & quality loop
bullets: Customer self-service: reschedule, edit address, add information.
Automatic incident-reason classification, monthly top-5 corrective actions.

aside.title: Client applications
bullets: Performance — aggressive caching, pagination, lazy-loading.
Reliability — offline mode, error recovery, client telemetry.
Security — device attestation, deeplink hardening.

aside.title: Team
bullets: Run — one N2 support engineer on light on-call.
Build — one full-stack developer on automation.
Rituals — weekly ops review, bi-weekly bug triage.

sections.title: Risks & mitigations
sections.subtitle: The structural risks identified, and the countermeasure for each.
rows: Document, delegate, rotating on-call, per-domain runbooks.
Delivery monitoring, channel fallback, vendor redundancy.
Load testing, light autoscaling, query and pricing pre-computation.
Clear per-domain ownership, normalised event contracts.
